paragraphs: Rav Chasa. In Ketubot 85b, Rav Nachman calls him Chasa. In Yevamot 121b, Rav Nachman says, “By God! [The fish have eaten] Chasa.” In Bava Metzia (compare 57a), Rav Nachman says, “Then Rav Chasa said ...,” etc.

notes.text: The supplied oath phrase is garbled as אפילוכוורא לחסא. The consulted Yevamot paragraph explicitly says “The fish have eaten Chasa,” supplied in brackets. Chasa is not silently changed to Chisda.

The saved whole Davidson Yevamot121b paragraph explicitly has Rav Nachman and אכלו כוורי לחסא, the fish have eaten Chasa, against supplied אפילו כוורא לחסא. Brackets mark contextual English supplementation, not a Hebrew repair or proved corruption history. Chasa is not Chisda. Rav Nachman is explicit for this Yevamot occurrence; the uninspected Ketubot and Bava Metzia title occurrences remain R' Nachman. Their conventional locators and הדר אמר quotation boundary stay qualified, and the supplied full Rav Chasa heading is restored in the body.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 936) cites Bava Metzia 56a, while the supplied transcription gives 57a. The consulted Bava Metzia 57a has the matching statement: Rav Nachman reports that Rav Chasa went on to report Rabbi Ami’s answer. Ketubot 85b also explicitly names Rav Nachman, and Rashi there points to Chasa’s drowning in Yevamot 121b. Hyman’s print gives אפילו כוורא לחסא in the oath; the bracketed English follows the consulted Yevamot reading.
